Which of the following statements are true concerning the function $y=f(x)$ whose graph is shown above?  

I. ${lim}_{x\to \,-{3}^{+}}f(x)=0$

II. ${lim}_{x\to \,-{1}^{+}}f(x)=\text{DNE}$

III. ${lim}_{x\to \,-{1}^{-}}f(x)={lim}_{x\to \,{1}^{+}}f(x)$
question.worked_solution:
Let's look at each statement in turn.

- Statement I is true. As $x$ approaches $-3$ from the right, the function value $f(x)$ approaches $y=0,$ Therefore,

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,-{3}^{+}}f(x)=0\,.
$$

- Statement II is true. As $x$ approaches $-1$ from the right, the function value $f(x)$ is undefined, Therefore,

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,-{1}^{+}}f(x)=\text{DNE}\,.
$$

- Statement III is false. As $x$ approaches $-1$ from the left, the function value $f(x)$ approaches $y=-2$, and consequently

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,-{1}^{-}}f(x)=-2\,.
$$

Similarly, as $x$ approaches $1$ from the right, the function value $f(x)$ approaches $y=0$, and consequently

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,{1}^{+}}f(x)=0\,.
$$

 Therefore,

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,-{1}^{-}}f(x)\ne {lim}_{x\to \,{1}^{+}}f(x)\,.
$$

Therefore, only statements I and II are true.
